description: Contests, game shows, and award ceremonies held at DEF CON 33, including Hacker Jeopardy, Whose Slide Is It Anyway, and the annual Pwnie Awards.

talks.title: Hacker Jeopardy: Friday Night
talks.teaser: The Friday night edition of Hacker Jeopardy at DEF CON 33, featuring intense cybersecurity trivia, obscure hacker lore, and adult beverages.
talks.summary:
In this legendary Friday night contest from DEF CON 33, contestants and a packed audience gather for the riotous, uncensored tradition of Hacker Jeopardy. Opening at 00:00, the emcees kick off the game, establishing the irreverent ground rules where contestants wager points and face boisterous drinking penalties for incorrect responses.

At 23:01, teams battle through challenging and obscure trivia categories spanning network protocols, obscure hardware architectures, hacking history, and convention lore, accompanied by energetic audience participation and banter. At 46:00, the host introduces hilarious sponsor punishments and prizes, testing contestants' technical knowledge under pressure.

As competition intensifies past 01:09:02, contestants deliberate over high-stakes Double Jeopardy clues and custom hardware gadgets. Concluding at 01:32:01 with unique badge showcases (including the Tipsy Badge from Hacker Warehouse) and the Final Jeopardy showdown, the session captures the chaotic camaraderie and intellectual wit of one of DEF CON's longest-running traditions. talks.title: Hacker Jeopardy: Saturday Night
talks.teaser: The Saturday night championship round of Hacker Jeopardy at DEF CON 33, testing the brightest minds in infosec across high-stakes categories.
talks.summary:
DEF CON's irreverent classic tournament Hacker Jeopardy takes the stage for its marquee Saturday Night edition, pitting costumed teams of security researchers against one another in an evening of high-energy trivia and drinking penalties [05:45].

Contestants navigate challenging and esoteric trivia categories spanning computer history, cryptography, network protocols, operating systems, and pop-culture hacker lore [00:06, 10:52]. Highlights include rounds testing knowledge of historical ciphers—from classic Caesar shifts to 15th-century polyalphabetic cryptosystems [11:10]—alongside spirited buzzer battles, audience interactions, and rapid-fire penalty rounds that showcase the festive community atmosphere of DEF CON night events [24:23, 01:07:35].

talks.title: Whose Slide Is It Anyway?
talks.teaser: Hacker contestants improvise technical presentations on the fly using completely unfamiliar and absurd slide decks at DEF CON 33.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses.
